- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model is overly conservative.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted in early forecast windows — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts.
- After sharp price spikes, model forecasts tend to overcorrect downward — suppress immediate drop corrections if sentiment remains positive.
- Mean reversion bias: model often assumes prices return to historical mean too quickly — adjust for longer-term sentiment trends.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive, model fails to fully capture momentum — increase forecast slope slightly beyond historical trend.
- In low-volatility periods, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–3% buffer for negative sentiment spikes.
